title: row11
live_proof: host ASan on the 2026-10-16 trigger: heap-use-after-free, 0 bytes inside a freed 8-byte region, with the memcmp interceptor as frame 0 and fts3SegReaderCmp (sqlite3.c:160670) as frame 1; the region is the pending-terms hash key, allocated by fts3HashMalloc <- sqlite3Fts3HashInsert <- fts3PendingTermsAddOne <- fts3InsertTerms and freed by fts3HashFree <- sqlite3Fts3HashClear <- sqlite3Fts3PendingTermsClear <- fts3DoOptimize. The aliasing line is ext/fts3/fts3_write.c:1333, where fts3SegReaderNext copies the doclist into its own buffer but points zTerm straight at the hash key. Fixed upstream in 3.37.0
object: the pending-terms hash key memory that pReader->zTerm aliases
lifetime_ender: an optimize() during the scan frees the pending-terms hash
fidelity: real consumer, real allocator: a non-empty pending-terms hash, a scan open over it, and optimize() run mid-scan -- plus two ingredients the earlier trigger lacked, each necessary and each measured. The inserts must be in an UNCOMMITTED transaction, because every commit runs sqlite3Fts3PendingTermsFlush, which clears the hash. Some rows must be COMMITTED first, so the phrase's cursor holds a segment reader beside the pending one: zTerm is read only when terms are compared BETWEEN readers, and the per-row advance sqlite3Fts3MsrIncrNext compares docids only -- for a pending reader it even copies the position list into pMsr->aBuffer, upstream copying everything on this path except the term. NEEDS its own build group (fts3P, -DSQLITE_ENABLE_FTS3_PARENTHESIS) for the query shape that produces the restart

status: re-measured 2026-10-16 on the replaced trigger: host ASan reports the use-after-free; virtual-malloc MISSED with both controls as declared, and the probe shows it reached, compared the freed key and completed; virtual-nested-pools CAUGHT, cause=25 at the memcmp the comparison performs, attributed by function, with both controls as declared; cheribsd-revocation MISSED, RETURNED rc=0, with the boot's positive control trapping and the probe showing the same pointer identity. This arm's Sublet cell changes from not-detected to detected, which raises the study's Sublet count, so it is the direction to check hardest: it rests on the host ASan report, the cause-25 fault at the declared site, and a probe trace that is identical on three platforms. The arms block below is still the 2026-10-11 bundle's and is regenerated by derive-verdicts.py when this review ends
note: TRIGGER REPLACED 2026-10-16, after review found the recorded one could not reach the defect. The 2026-10-11 note had the first obstacle right -- each INSERT auto-commits, so the pending hash is empty when the scan opens -- but fixing only that is not enough, and three iterations of host-ASan variants (15 shapes, all silent) were needed to find why. With the inserts in an open transaction the aliasing does happen (probe site 47 prints it), and the mid-scan optimize() does free the hash with the reader still alive, yet nothing reads the key afterwards: a single-term lookup reader holds a COPY of the doclist, and zTerm is read only by term comparisons, which run before the first row. What reaches it is a RESTART after the clear: fts3EvalRestart -> fts3EvalPhraseStart -> fts3EvalPhraseLoad -> fts3TermSelect steps the EXISTING Fts3MultiSegReader again, and fts3SegReaderStart sorts the readers with fts3SegReaderCmp, which memcmps the dangling zTerm. The restart is reached the way case 06 reaches it, through offsets() over a NEAR group under an OR whose AND operand to the left fails first. Hence (xx AND (apple NEAR/3 qq)) OR pendingone with two rows committed and two pending. This case is NOT a duplicate of case 06: the object is the hash key rather than a merged poslist, the read is a term comparison rather than the offsets loop, upstream fixed them separately (3.37.0 against 3.49.0), and this access happens INSIDE the restart, so it strictly precedes case 06's. Probe site 47 prints the alias, the clear and the comparison with their pointers: the same key pointer is aliased, freed and compared on native memsys5, on virtual Capstone with lookaside off, and on CheriBSD purecap. witnesses=0 everywhere because the optimize allocates heavily right after the free and memsys5 reissues the block, the blind spot case 05 documented; the pointer identity is the evidence. Tooling defect found on the way: cheribsd/build-corpus-cheri.sh keys its cached probe engine object on the defines and the amalgamation's FILE NAME, not its contents, so a second probe source at a different path silently reuses the first object -- the site-47 binary came back carrying site 46's hooks and printed nothing. Caught because the binary held no site=47 strings; the object must be removed by hand between probe sources until the key includes the source hash
fault_sites_why: host ASan on the 2026-10-16 trigger reports the read with the memcmp interceptor as frame 0 and fts3SegReaderCmp as frame 1 (sqlite3.c:160670, memcmp(pLhs->zTerm, pRhs->zTerm, ...)): the stale load is the comparison itself, which libc performs. Both names are declared, the same convention cases 13, 14, 17 and 19 use for binCollFunc/memcmp and sqlite3VdbeSerialPut/memcpy, because the runners resolve only the faulting pc's symbol. Probe site 47 pins the caller independently: it prints the aliased key pointer, the clear that frees that same pointer, and the comparison that reads it
